---
title: "tellurix"
subtitle: "Differentiable telluric absorption for high-resolution spectra"
toc: false
page-layout: full

Every ground-based spectrum is the source multiplied by the transmission of Earth's atmosphere. **tellurix** computes that transmission line by line, from the molecules' laboratory line parameters and the atmosphere's pressure, temperature and composition at the time of observation. It then fits it to the observed spectrum and divides it out.

It is written in [JAX](https://github.com/jax-ml/jax) on top of [ExoJAX](https://github.com/HajimeKawahara/exojax). The whole model, from line opacity to detector pixels, is therefore one compiled, differentiable function: it runs on a GPU and returns exact gradients for fitting. [LBLRTM](https://github.com/AER-RCG/LBLRTM), the standard atmospheric line-by-line code, is its accuracy reference.

![Sky transmission over the IGRINS H and K bands at R = 45,000, total and molecule by molecule, computed by tellurix for an ERA5 atmosphere over Gemini South at air mass 1.5.](figures/output/fig_intro_transmission.png){width=100%}

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Accurate

Given the same atmospheric layers, tellurix matches LBLRTM 12.17 to **0.010% median and 0.039% at the 99th percentile** at R = 45,000. It uses AER Line File 3.9, the MT_CKD 4.3 water continuum, pressure shifts and first-order CO₂ line coupling.

![](figures/output/fig_lblrtm_5000.png){width=100%}

[Validation against LBLRTM →](manuscript/04-validation-against-lblrtm.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Fast and differentiable

Reverse-mode autodiff gives the gradient of the fit objective with respect to every parameter in one pass. With the opacity precomputed, a gradient costs a few milliseconds on one GPU, **about 240× faster** than the finite differences an LBLRTM-based fit needs.

![](figures/output/fig_performance_gradient.png){width=100%}

[Fitting and computational cost →](manuscript/03-fitting-and-computational-cost.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### IGRINS

Per-order fits of A0V standards from Gemini South, DCT and McDonald reach about **1.3σ on a dry night**. A night calibration then corrects science targets with only one water scale and one velocity per frame.

![](figures/output/fig_igrins_standard.png){width=100%}

[Application to IGRINS →](manuscript/06-application-to-igrins.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### FTS atlases

The whole Arcturus infrared atlas (598 page-epochs, 0.91–5.4 µm) and the NSO Kitt Peak solar atlases are corrected. Each spectrum's instrumental profile is measured from its own interferogram envelope.

![](figures/output/fig_arcturus_typical.png){width=100%}

[Application to FTS atlases →](manuscript/05-application-to-fts-atlases.qmd)
:::

:::

## How it works

![](figures/diagrams/model_composition.png){width=100%}

The atmosphere, line opacity and continuum are interchangeable components. Together they give the transmission, which an observation model turns into detector pixels: stellar spectrum, Doppler shifts, line-spread function, pixel integration and a smooth continuum. A bounded fit then adjusts a handful of parameters: one column scale per gas, the velocity, the line-spread-function width and the continuum. The [forward-model chapter](manuscript/02-the-forward-model.qmd) explains each step from first principles and compares it with LBLRTM's implementation.

## Packages

The repository is a workspace of three packages. The core knows no instrument; instrument packages build on it.

| Package | Import | What it contains |
|---|---|---|
| `tellurix` | `tellurix` | Forward model, line opacity, MT_CKD and O₂ continua, fitter, stellar source, site profiles, run records, LBLRTM reference tooling |
| `tellurix-fts` | `tellurix_fts` | Readers for the Arcturus and NSO solar FTS atlases, interferogram-based instrument profiles, the solar window fit |
| `tellurix-igrins` | `tellurix_igrins` | IGRINS reduced-spectrum reader, night calibration, lamp-flat blaze, the per-order standard-star fit |

## Get started

```bash
git clone https://github.com/leejjoon/tellurix.git
cd tellurix
uv sync --dev --extra gpu        # Python 3.10; omit --extra gpu for CPU only
uv run tellurix-download-data all  # AER Line File 3.9 and MT_CKD 4.3, SHA-256 checked
```

See [Getting started](getting-started.qmd) for a first transmission spectrum in about twenty lines.

## Status and citation

tellurix is research software under active development, and a paper describing it is in preparation; its [working draft](manuscript/index.qmd) is on this site. To cite a released version of the code and its fitted products, use the Zenodo record [10.5281/zenodo.23121556](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23121556), which covers all versions.
